mood.label: Playful Quiet Solidarity
mood.summary: A sunny neighborhood march finds a new kind of fun when the children make space for a sleeping baby.

storyteller.quirk: Keeps the same marching pulse as the words soften from stomp to tiptoe.

kid_older.quirk: Counts the quiet steps aloud once, then counts the next steps on their fingers.

kid_younger.quirk: Finishes each parade call with an extra-big silent wave.

art.line: Round contours pressed into clay with shallow incised seams.
art.lighting: Soft afternoon light from one side catches the raised glaze.
art.composition: Broad rows of sidewalk tiles guide the eye from lifted heels to patting hands to waving fingers. Keep faces and gestures large.
art.style_prompt_prefix: Children’s picture-book illustration built from hand-modeled glazed ceramic relief tiles, rounded clay silhouettes, broad matte sidewalk tiles, soft afternoon light, and clear expressive faces.

qa.intro_hook: Hold up your hands like a parade conductor. Can you show us a beat without making a sound?
qa.outro_hook: Conduct our last three moves together. Tiptoe, pat your knees softly, and wave to the baby’s window.

kid_notes.kid_older: Invite them to conduct the tiptoe, pat, wave sequence and explain how it helps the baby stay asleep.
kid_notes.kid_younger: Show one move at a time and welcome a finger tiptoe, a soft knee pat, or a silent wave.

sound.music_direction: Use softly plucked strings for a small marching tune. Keep the pulse when the parade changes, then leave room for a full silent beat at the baby’s window.

rationale: The march keeps its rhythm as the children change how they move, so the read-aloud lets young viewers feel how making room for someone can keep the fun going. Raised ceramic shapes make the quieter gestures easy to see.
